In 1876 Elisha Gray invented the Musical Telegraph, and in 1906 the audion vacuum tube made signal generation and amplification possible. In 1940 Sachs placed electronic instruments in the fifth Hornbostel–Sachs class, and in the twenty-first century they are widely used in most musical styles.

An electronic instrument makes sound with electronic circuits, usually outputting an audio signal that is sounded through an amplifier and loudspeakers; the player sets pitch, frequency and duration with a keyboard, controller or synthesis module, and the interface and the sound-producing device can be separated by a musical performance description language. It belongs to the fifth Hornbostel–Sachs class, electrophones, number 53, meaning instruments that sound mainly through electrical oscillators. Modern players use them widely, and in pop recordings such as electronic dance music bass synthesisers, synthesisers and drum machines are common.
電子樂器的操作以使用者介面為主，常見為鍵盤，也可使用控制器或無接觸方式。演奏者調: An electronic instrument is played mainly through a user interface, commonly a keyboard, but also a controller or a contactless means. The player sets the pitch, frequency or duration, the signal goes to a synthesis module, a computer or another electronic or digital sound generator, and a power amplifier drives loudspeakers. A beginner must become familiar with connecting the controller to a separate sound-producing device, for example by Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) or Open Sound Control; with the theremin, the practice is to control the sound without touching the instrument. A solid-state keyboard feels and responds differently from a mechanical piano keyboard, so it is best to begin with the parameters of a single note.
電子樂器的音色由電子電路或數位音訊信號產生，經功率放大器驅動喇叭播出；演奏者可透: The timbre of an electronic instrument is generated by electronic circuits or a digital audio signal and played through loudspeakers driven by a power amplifier; the player sets pitch, frequency and note duration through an interface such as a keyboard or controller. Under Hornbostel–Sachs 53 the sound comes mainly from electrically driven oscillators, unlike class 51, electroacoustic instruments, and class 52, electro-mechanical instruments. The Telharmonium used tone wheels for additive synthesis, combining notes and overtones with control of dynamic level; the theremin can be played without touching the instrument. Simple electronic instruments are sometimes called sound effects, and the line between them and real instruments is not clear-cut.
